translations.text: And from the sound of their voices there came a great, clear river, as though from a small spring.
In the third year of his reign, the king gave a banquet for his friends and nobles, and also for others from the peoples of Persia and Media and for all the rulers and provincial governors.

It was decorated with fine linen and cotton cloth, which had been arranged and secured with cords of purple and fine linen and fastened to gold and purple capitals that stood on precious columns and golden bases. There were many gold and silver seats, inlaid with pearls and precious stones and furnished with coverings, multicolored designs, and costly fabrics, in the rose-paved courtyard.
And the king’s servants said, “Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.”

And two of the king’s eunuchs, who were chief guards of the people, became distressed because they were jealous of Mordecai, whom the king honored more than them, and they wanted to kill King Artaxerxes.
After this, King Artaxerxes honored Haman, together with Dathuba and his companions, and raised him to the foremost seat above all his friends.

And he spoke to the king and said, “There is a people scattered among the nations throughout your kingdom. They are more wicked and deceitful than all other peoples, and they do not obey the royal laws. It is of no benefit to the king if you let them remain.”
“Now, if it pleases the king, give an order to destroy them, and I will deposit ten thousand talents of silver in the royal treasury.”

And the royal scribes were summoned in the first month, on the thirteenth day. As Haman commanded them, they wrote a letter to the military commanders and governors throughout all the provinces, from India to Ethiopia, one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, and to the rulers of the peoples, each in its own language, by order of Artaxerxes.

“Go and gather the Jews who are in the city of Susa, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, either by day or by night. My maids and I will also take care to fast, and then I will go in to the king. Although doing this is contrary to the king’s laws, I will do it; and even if I must die, I will not delay.”
And now, Lord, we have sinned before you, and you have delivered us into the hands of our enemies.
But save us with your uplifted arm, and help me, who am alone and have no helper except you, Lord.
And your maidservant has not eaten from Haman’s table, nor have I honored the king’s drinking feasts, nor have I drunk the wine of their sacrifices.
